skill.name: runlater
skill.description: Schedule HTTP requests with RunLater. Use when someone wants a URL or webhook called at an exact time or on a cron schedule, needs a job their host limits (for example Vercel Hobby's daily cron), wants to pause or run a scheduled request, or asks why a scheduled request failed.
skill.summary: Schedule public HTTP requests, manage recurring jobs, and inspect execution results through RunLater MCP tools.
skill.author: runlater-app

content.value_statement: Hosting limits can make scheduled HTTP tasks difficult to manage. This skill guides connected RunLater MCP tools to schedule requests, manage jobs, and inspect failures.
actual_capabilities: Schedule GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE requests once or on a recurring cron schedule.
Use IANA timezones and report the next run time returned by the scheduling tool.
List schedules and inspect recent status codes, durations, and response previews.
Run requests immediately with agreement for endpoints that have side effects.
Pause, resume, or permanently delete schedules with confirmation before deletion.
Check account plan, limits, and usage through the account_status tool.
limitations: Requires a connected RunLater MCP service; this skill contains instructions, not a standalone scheduler.
Only public URLs are supported; private and local addresses are refused.
Cron schedules run at most once per minute.
Workspaces without a plan can connect and read, but cannot schedule or run requests.

use_cases.title: Schedule application maintenance
use_cases.description: Schedule a public maintenance endpoint when hosting cron limits do not meet the required frequency.

use_cases.title: Investigate failed scheduled requests
use_cases.description: Inspect recent response previews, status codes, and durations, then pause a failing schedule while investigating.

use_cases.title: Arrange a one-time webhook
use_cases.description: Schedule an authorized webhook for a specific time and confirm the timezone and next execution time.

prompt_templates.title: View scheduled jobs
prompt_templates.prompt: List my RunLater schedules and show my account plan, limits, and usage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect existing schedules without changing them.

prompt_templates.title: Schedule one public request
prompt_templates.prompt: Schedule a GET to [public URL] on [date] at [time] in [IANA timezone]. Confirm the next run time.

prompt_templates.title: Create a recurring webhook
prompt_templates.prompt: Schedule a POST to [public URL] with [cron expression] in [IANA timezone]. Use my authorized authentication header. Ask before testing it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create an authenticated recurring request.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate and control a failing job
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect recent runs for [schedule ID]. Summarize status codes, durations, and response previews. Pause it if failures persist. Ask before running it immediately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: diagnose failures and manage an existing schedule.

output_examples.input: Schedule a request at 9am tomorrow, but I have not provided a timezone.
output_examples.output: Which IANA timezone should I use for 9am, such as America/Chicago?

output_examples.input: Schedule a GET request to my localhost endpoint.
output_examples.output: RunLater requires a public URL and refuses local addresses. Provide a deployed endpoint or an authorized public tunnel URL.

output_examples.input: Test my scheduled webhook that creates an order.
output_examples.output: Running this webhook now will send a real request and may create an order. Do you approve this immediate test?

best_practices: Specify an IANA timezone and verify the next run time returned by RunLater.
Use headers for endpoint secrets and verify the destination before sharing credentials.
Confirm immediate tests with side effects and inspect execution results before relying on a schedule.
anti_patterns: Scheduling an ambiguous local time without confirming the timezone.
Running a state-changing request without agreement or deleting a schedule without confirmation.
Using non-idempotent endpoints without considering retries after responses outside the 2xx range.

faq.question: What must be connected before using this skill?
faq.answer: The RunLater MCP tools must be available. This skill provides instructions, not the service implementation.

faq.question: Which HTTP methods are supported?
faq.answer: The documented tools support GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests.

faq.question: Can I schedule requests to localhost?
faq.answer: No. RunLater requires public URLs and refuses private and local addresses.

faq.question: How often can a recurring request run?
faq.answer: Cron schedules run at most once per minute. Use an IANA timezone to specify the intended local time.

faq.question: How are authentication secrets supplied?
faq.answer: Pass endpoint secrets as headers. The instructions state that tools return header names, not values; the external implementation was not reviewed.

faq.question: What happens when a scheduled request fails?
faq.answer: Responses outside the 2xx range count as failures and are retried. Inspect recent runs for status codes, durations, and response previews.
